summary: Claude was substantially more accurate on this back-right three-quarter view. It correctly identified the prominent end-on brass cylinder gear (which codex missed entirely) and placed all three visible base corners and all three visible top-frame corners on the true corners with machine-relative names consistent with a back-right camera (nearest corner = back-right, image-left = back-left, image-right = front-right). Codex's systematic error was a left/right mirror of every analyzer corner name, compounded on the base by dots floating off the actual corners (on top edges / mid-rim) and by calling two visible corners occluded while marking two truly-occluded far corners as visible. The only point codex won was the lower rocker-arm tip corner, and the tips overall are a near-tie.
